entities.summary:
AT&T Inc. is an American multinational telecommunications conglomerate headquartered in Dallas, Texas, tracing its origins to Alexander Graham Bell's telephone patent of 1876 and the American Telephone & Telegraph Company founded in 1885. Once the world's largest company and the sole provider of telephone service across much of the United States, AT&T's history spans the entire arc of modern telecommunications.

The Bell System's 1956 Consent Decree and 1982 antitrust breakup into seven 'Baby Bell' regional companies was the largest corporate breakup in American history, creating independent telecommunications companies across US regions. The reconsolidation of AT&T through acquisitions of SBC Communications (2005) and BellSouth (2006) essentially reassembled much of the original Bell System. AT&T then diversified into satellite TV (DirecTV, 2015) and entertainment through the $85 billion Time Warner acquisition (2018, renamed WarnerMedia), before spinning off WarnerMedia in 2022.

AT&T's Bell Laboratories, operating 1925-1996, was the most productive industrial research laboratory in history: transistors, lasers, solar cells, cellular networks, UNIX operating system, C programming language, and information theory all emerged from Bell Labs. The lab's innovations created the digital age before AT&T's antitrust breakup scattered its researchers.
